reports.desc: The page on Facebook said free puppies which they misspelled the name shih tzu as shitzu.  I was interested and asked questions.  At first they said $500 then I said I can't pay that for any dog.  They changed it to $150.  They said I had to send a deposit of $75.  Which I was stupid and sent them $75.  We were to meet later in week.  The next day after taking $75 they asked for $75 more for vaccinations.  That's when I said no.  That's when I realized it was a scam.  These people may live anywhere because they said Louisville KY but they may be in Africa.  I reported to Facebook but they say they don't break the community standards.  So they don't care if it is a scam, and take people's money and give them nothing in return.  I hope you can stop this and I saw more than one of these on Facebook.

I saw a targeted ad from a company called Mayberry North Carolina with beautiful clothes on Facebook.  The ad showed a cute storefront, claimed to be based in North Carolina and was running a sale.  I didn’t click the Facebook link, but rather did a search for the company and it took me to the same website with the cute storefront.  I ordered a suit and a top. Paid via credit card.  Received numerous updates that shipping is taking longer than normal.  When I tried to track the shipment, I saw something about international customs.  That was my red flag and I immediately dug deeper and saw this is a scam operation from china posing as a cute clothing shop in North Carolina. Since October 2025, I have received nearly 600 unsolicited prerecorded calls promoting supposed personal loans/debt relief. I have NEVER applied for a loan, answered these calls, returned a call, or consented to these solicitations. The callers continually rotate/spoof caller-ID numbers while directing recipients to recurring callback numbers using fictitious stories. Recent messages claim I have an existing “file,” that supervisors/underwriters have reviewed it, and, often lately, that numerous employees have repeatedly tried to reach me. This caller offered unsolicited "time sensitive resolution options" to my supposedly unpaid taxes. I don't owe any taxes. Other recordings use similar fictitious personal stories and loan approvals. I have preserved numerous voicemails, screenshots, dates, caller-ID numbers and callback numbers and have reported this to the FTC numerous times. This appears to be a large-scale, persistent robocall campaign, not isolated calls.
